title: Oath and Thorn
premise: Oscar Sandoval has spent his life in Thornvale, a valley where magic cannot enter, carving the bones of the dead and listening to their last whispers. When he finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old prophecy, he learns his soul was sold before his birth to the court beneath Mount Cindrel—and that the debt comes due at moonset. To reclaim it, he must leave the valley's protection for the first time, guided by a disgraced oath-keeper named Wren and the voices of the dead who remember the original bargain. In the bone courts below, Oscar discovers the prophecy's author was his own grandmother, who traded his soul to buy the valley its magic-free sanctuary; in the end, Oscar shatters the contract by offering the court something rarer than a soul—his gift of hearing the dead—freeing himself but binding him forever to carry the mountain's voices home.
about_author: Elodie Montrose is a former mortuary archivist who turned to fantasy after years of cataloguing epitaphs left her hungry for stories about what the living owe the dead. She writes from a farmhouse full of rescued animals and inherited furniture, none of which she is allowed to replace.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Supposed to Exist
chapters.summary: Oscar Sandoval carves a memorial bone while the dead murmur their usual fragments—until one voice names him. At the chapel archive, he finds a prophecy book dated a century back, and today's date circled in faded ink beside his own name. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: quiet dread cracking open an ordinary life.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Oscar tests the valley's edge, where magic dies at an invisible line, and confirms the whispers grow louder beyond it. His aunt Maren admits she has always known about the prophecy and forbids him to leave. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the suffocating love of protection that feels like imprisonment.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Bone Gate
chapters.summary: Wren Ashgrave arrives seeking the 'hearing carver,' exiled from the mountain court for failing an oath. She reveals Oscar's soul was collateral in a bargain struck before his birth—the price of Thornvale's sanctuary. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into desperate purpose.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Comparing script, Oscar realizes the prophecy's author was his grandmother Ilsa, who vanished into the mountain decades ago. Her marginal notes describe a soul-debt and a way to void it—if he reaches the court before moonset on the marked date. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: inheritance as both wound and map.

chapters.title: Leaving Thornvale
chapters.summary: At dawn Oscar crosses the boundary line; magic floods him like cold water, and the dead become deafening. He nearly turns back until his mother's voice—one of the dead—urges him onward. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: grief transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: The Toll Road
chapters.summary: On the pilgrim road, Wren teaches him court etiquette: never give your true name, never accept a gift. They are robbed by hollow-eyed tollmen who serve the mountain, and Oscar hears the tollmen's stolen souls screaming. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the cost of the world outside the valley.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Sheltering in a ruined monastery, they find Ilsa's travel journal hidden in a reliquary, detailing her own journey down—and her growing horror at what the court wanted. The final pages are torn out. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: intimacy with a grandmother he barely knew.

chapters.title: The Court of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: A border town under the mountain's shadow shows Oscar what soul-debts do: children born pledged, elders hollowed into servants. A dying woman begs him to hear her last words, and he does—for free. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: compassion hardening into anger.

chapters.title: What Wren Broke
chapters.summary: Wren confesses her broken oath: she was ordered to deliver a child to the court and refused, losing her name, rank, and magic. Oscar realizes she sees her failure repeated in him. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: shame met, at last, with forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Gate of Teeth
chapters.summary: They reach the mountain's mouth, guarded by a gate carved from the jaws of an ancient beast that demands a memory as toll. Oscar pays it a memory of his mother's face—his most precious possession. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: sacrifice as proof of intent.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Below, the dead are not whispers but a chorus, and Oscar can barely walk for the noise. Wren leads them through bone-lit galleries toward the audience hall, evoking patrols of veined, marble-skinned courtiers. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: terror disciplined into focus.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Souls
chapters.summary: In the archive hall, Oscar finds the ledger bearing his entry: 'Sandoval, Oscar—one soul, held in trust.' Beside it, Ilsa's signature and a clause neither of them noticed: the debt transfers to any heir who reads this page. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Audience with the Pale Regent
chapters.summary: Dragged before the Pale Regent, Oscar bargains for his soul; the Regent offers it freely—in exchange for his hearing, which the court covets above all souls. He refuses and is thrown into the holding dark. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: defiance priced in suffering.

chapters.title: The Holding Dark
chapters.summary: Imprisoned among the pledged, Oscar uses his gift to ease the dying and learns the court's secret: the Regent is starving, sustained only by harvested souls, and Ilsa's bargain bought Thornvale with time, not permanence. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: pity for the monster.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Last Page
chapters.summary: Wren infiltrates the archive and recovers the torn journal pages: Ilsa planned to void the debt by giving the court her death willingly—but died before she could, leaving the contract half-made and transferable. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: hope found in an unfinished act of love.

chapters.title: Moonset Approaches
chapters.summary: With hours left, Wren breaks Oscar out through the ossuary galleries; the dead guide them, whispering paths only he can hear. The Regent senses the theft and wakes the court. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: breathless flight powered by borrowed courage.

chapters.title: The Bargain Reversed
chapters.summary: Cornered at the Ledger, Oscar offers the Regent not his soul but a new covenant: his hearing, freely given each year at moonset, so the court may feed without harvesting. The Regent, weary of hunger, accepts—and the old contract burns away. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: turning corruption into covenant.

chapters.title: The Regent's True Face
chapters.summary: As the pact seals, the Regent's glamour fails, revealing a starved, ancient figure who was once the valley's first guardian, corrupted by the court it built. It thanks Oscar with terrible gentleness. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: horror braided with mercy.

chapters.title: Climbing Toward Morning
chapters.summary: They ascend as the mountain groans, the freed pledges following the sound of Oscar's voice like a lantern. Some make it; some do not, and Oscar carries their last words up with him. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: survival that refuses to feel like victory.

chapters.title: Crossing Back
chapters.summary: At the valley line, Oscar hesitates—crossing means the annual journey to the mountain begins, and his gift will change Thornvale forever. His mother's voice tells him to come home anyway. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: choosing a burden over an escape.

chapters.title: The Hearing Carver
chapters.summary: Thornvale receives its changed son: now the valley's dead can be heard, mourned properly, and laid to rest. Maren grieves what he lost; Oscar begins teaching others to listen. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: grief settling into purpose.

chapters.title: First Moonset
chapters.summary: One year later, Oscar walks to the mountain at moonset to keep his covenant, Wren at his side, and finds the Regent waiting—not as a jailer but as a penitent. The dead sing, and for the first time, Oscar sings back. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as a promise kept.
